content.p: Milton Orkopoulos was a Labor member of the New South Wales Parliament who held the Swansea electorate from 1999 until he resigned in November 2006. He later served as Aboriginal affairs minister. In November 2006 he was charged with child sex and drug offences and left Parliament, and between 2008 and 2023 he was convicted in two separate criminal trials. In November 2023 a judge in the NSW District Court handed him up to 20 years in prison, and set 13 years as the non-parole period. He has continued to deny sexually abusing underage boys.
content.h2: A councillor who became a minister
content.p: Before entering Parliament, Orkopoulos sat on the Lake Macquarie council. An ABC report from June 2020 described him as a councillor for four years. In 1999 he won Swansea for Labor. In 2005 he was given the Aboriginal affairs portfolio, which he held under Premier Morris Iemma until 2006, according to the Sydney Morning Herald. According to a December 2019 ABC report, his victims came into contact with him through his political role, at a Labor function and through work experience he offered in his electoral office.

The case reached the public in November 2006. Orkopoulos was arrested the week before he resigned from Parliament, and he faced 30 charges, including child sex and drug offences, the Sydney Morning Herald reported. Iemma sacked him from cabinet before the formal charges were laid, and Labor moved to expel him from the party. On 13 November 2006 he resigned as the member for Swansea with immediate effect. He said he was innocent of any wrongdoing.

The affair also drew in other politicians. Upper house Labor member Jan Burnswoods said in a statutory declaration that Orkopoulos had told her two coalition MPs, Adrian Piccoli and Andrew Constance, had warned him he was under investigation. Both men denied the claim. Iemma said that police should look into reports that two Labor members, Bryce Gaudry and John Mills, had known about allegations before the arrest. Mills publicly denied being told.

The first trial was heard in Newcastle. On 14 March 2008 the jury found Orkopoulos guilty on 28 of the 29 charges it had deliberated on, the Sydney Morning Herald reported. The jury of six men and five women took a little more than a day to reach its verdict. The three men who testified said he gave them cannabis before making sexual advances, and one said he had got him hooked on heroin and then demanded sexual favours to clear a drug debt. The court also heard that Orkopoulos regularly met one of the boys for sex late at night at the Swansea electorate office.

He was taken into custody straight after the verdict and refused bail. At sentencing, Judge Ralph Coolahan told the court that Orkopoulos had leveraged his standing to gain the confidence of the boys, and he called the conduct "premeditated, predatory and manipulative with far-reaching impacts", as the Newcastle Herald reported in 2020. The sentence was handed down in May 2008. The Newcastle Herald put the maximum at 13 years and eight months, and the non-parole period at nine years and three months.

Orkopoulos appealed in 2009. The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal dismissed his appeal against conviction, the Newcastle Herald reported on 25 August, but its three-judge panel gave him leave to appeal the sentence. The court took three months off the maximum, and the paper reported the new terms as a maximum of 13 years and eight months, and a non-parole period of nine years. The three justices described him as "entirely unconvincing" in his evidence about contact with one of the boys. Phone records were put before the court, and he said someone else must have been using his mobile phone to speak to the boy.

He was released from Long Bay prison on 20 December 2019, after serving more than 11 years. His conditions included electronic monitoring and a ban on approaching his victims. His parole had been delayed since 2017 because he had not completed a sex offender program, and he finished the program later.

In January 2020 he was arrested at a home in Malabar, in Sydney's south-east, and charged with two counts of failing to meet his reporting obligations as a registered child sex offender. The alleged breaches concerned a conversation with his granddaughter and an Instagram account that he had set up in his own name, according to ABC News. His parole was revoked in February 2020, and he was returned to custody.

In December 2020 Orkopoulos pleaded guilty to one reporting offence in the Local Court. Magistrate Philip Stewart imposed a two-year community correction order and said the court's power to impose the sentence was "fettered", because he had no power to impose a prison term. Stewart said he was "unable to find that he is unlikely to reoffend", the Greek Herald reported.

The bigger case was the new historical charges. On 15 June 2020 detectives arrested him at Silverwater jail and charged him with 15 offences over two boys in the 1990s, including aggravated sexual assault and causing a child to take part in child prostitution. Police said the offences took place in the Lake Macquarie area and on the NSW mid-north coast. In December 2020 six new charges were laid, relating to two alleged victims in Swansea and Belmont. Court documents also disclosed a count of trying to pervert the course of justice, over a statutory declaration, signed by an alleged victim, that retracted an allegation of sexual abuse. In February 2021 the State Parole Authority refused to reverse its decision to revoke his parole. In May 2021 he pleaded not guilty to 23 charges relating to the two alleged victims in Swansea and Belmont. Six charges were withdrawn at that hearing, according to the Greek Herald.

The trial over the four boys was heard in Sydney's Downing Centre District Court. On 5 April 2023 the jury found him guilty of 26 of the 28 charges he faced, and not guilty of one drug-supply count and one count of perverting the course of justice. The offences involved four boys and took place between 1993 and 2003, on the Mid North Coast and in the Lake Macquarie area. Of the 28 counts, the ABC listed eight for supplying a prohibited drug, eight for indecent assault and 11 for sexual intercourse with a person between 10 and 16. He had entered not guilty pleas to all of them.

During the trial he tried to have the charges dismissed by describing them as "fanciful" and "outrageously wrong", the Sydney Morning Herald reported. Prosecutors said he had a sexual interest in young boys which he acted on "time and time again".

On 6 June 2023 he was found with head injuries at the Metropolitan Special Programs Centre at Long Bay, according to a statement from Corrective Services NSW. He was taken to Prince of Wales Hospital and was reported to have head, body and leg injuries. ABC reporting in November 2023 said he had been hit from behind in June, with a fractured left ankle and injuries to his head and ribs, and that he had been assaulted twice in custody.
content.h2: The sentence and the victims' accounts
content.p: On 24 November 2023 Judge Jane Culver handed down the sentence. Orkopoulos appeared by video link. The maximum term was 20 years, with a non-parole period of 13 years. The judge said his offending against all the victims had been "calculated, predatory and manipulative", and that there was "no evidence of remorse or contrition". The ABC reported that the judge found special circumstances because his time in custody would be harder than usual, given his vulnerability to depression and the risk of institutionalisation.

The victims' impact statements described drug addiction, homelessness, time in prison, broken relationships and depression. In one statement a man said he had been in custody for most of his life since the age of 11. Judge Culver said such consequences were typical in cases of this kind, because child sexual assault "typically and tragically derails the lives of victims". His lawyers had argued that he would pose little threat to children on release, given the strict conditions and his age. He is first eligible for parole in June 2033.

Reports do not agree on every figure. The ABC and the Greek Herald described the 2023 case as involving four boys. The Newcastle Herald wrote that he was now convicted of sexually assaulting seven boys between 1995 and 2005. The ages of the boys also vary: the Greek Herald gave 10 to 15, the Sydney Morning Herald reported prosecutors describing boys aged 10 to 14, and the Newcastle Herald gave 10 to 17. The number of 2008 charges is given as 28 in the Sydney Morning Herald and the 2009 appeal report, and as 30 offences in the ABC's 2023 coverage. The non-parole period for the 2008 sentence is given as nine years and three months, and the 2009 appeal report gives nine years after the cut. The 2009 report also implies a longer 2008 maximum than the 13 years and eight months given in the other reports. For the 2020 charges, the Newcastle Herald and the ABC gave 15 offences in June 2020, while the Greek Herald reported 23 charges at a hearing in May 2021, after six more charges had been laid in December 2020. Each figure is given here as the outlet reported it.

Orkopoulos is in custody. He has been convicted in two trials, and the appeal court upheld the 2008 conviction in 2009, although it reduced the sentence slightly. He continues to deny sexually abusing underage boys. The Greek Herald reported that he is first eligible for parole in June 2033 and that his total sentence is set to expire in June 2040. The Newcastle Herald said he will be 77 when he becomes eligible.
